---
title: Owner-Based Access Controls
description: Define a Restricted Dataset for access control
---

## **Overview**

Owner-based Access Controls grant access based on whether a user is on the team that owns the asset or data. The owning team is determined from team tags: `team:{team}` for both assets and data. For logs and other data that support attribute-style tags, `@team` is recognized too.

A single ownership policy replaces a large number of per-team datasets and per-asset restriction policies — e.g. instead of hand-building one dataset per team, you write one policy that divides access by team responsibility across a product.

The behavior is slightly different depending on whether the controls are for *Data* or *Assets*. See How it works section below for the distinction.

## **What's changed in the UI**

![][image1]

If you previously used Data Access Control, note the following changes:

* The configuration page moved to **Access Control** in Organization Settings, replacing the former *Data Access Controls* item.  
* This page is now also where you configure Owner-based Access Policies for assets (such as monitors and dashboards).  
* Some terms were renamed:

| Previous term | New term |
| ----- | ----- |
| Restricted Dataset | **Sensitive Data Partition** |
| Unrestricted Access | **High Permission User Groups** |
| Data Restrictions / “Strict Mode” | **Products Hidden by Default** |

## **How it works**

The model differs slightly depending on the content type.

* **Data** — you only see the data tagged with your team(s).  
* **Assets** — you only get access (editor or viewer, depending on the policy configured) to the asset if you're on the team(s) the asset is tagged with. An *asset* is a resource such as a monitor or dashboard.

**Example:** If you create an OBAC policy for Logs and your team is payments, you can see log events tagged with `team:payments` or `@team:payments`. Log events without a matching team tag are not visible to you unless you are included in a High Permission User Group. For assets, the same ownership check applies to the asset itself: a dashboard tagged `team:payments` is accessible to members of the payments team according to the policy’s viewer/editor settings.

### **Assets can have both owner-based and record-level policies applied**

Record-level restriction policies can still exist alongside Owner-based policies. When an owner-based policy is in place, the user will see the following (in this example, for a dashboard with no record-level policy).

## **![][image2]**

The policy editor can then *expand* (not narrow down) access to more people by pressing “Share Access”. Owner-based and record-level policies combine **additively**.

Side note: *high permission user groups* don’t get displayed in the record-level Permissions modal by design.

## **The Access Control page**

To view and manage your policies, navigate to **Organization Settings** and select **Access Control** (Preview) under the **Access** heading. You must have the `user_access_manage` permission to make changes.

The **Access Restriction Policies** tab is organized into three sections:

1. **Access Policies** — a table of your policies, showing each policy's *Name*, *User Group*, *Restriction* (Viewing or Editing), *Content* (Data or Assets), *Product*, and *Matching Criteria*. Ownership policies show Owner Team as the user group and matching criteria; a Sensitive Data Partition shows its tag, such as `sensitivity:high`.  
2. **High Permission User Groups** — roles, teams, and users designated with broad access permissions. A user group here retains access regardless of policy boundaries.  
3. **Products Hidden by Default** — per-product configuration that hides a product's data by default until access is explicitly granted through a policy.

## **Create a policy**

![][image3]

1. Navigate to **Organization Settings** \> **Access Control** \> **Access Restriction Policies**.  
2. Click **New Policy**.  
3. **Policy Starting Points**  
   * **Access via Ownership** — divide access by team responsibility.  
   * **Sensitive Data Partition** — designate a data subset for use by certain people (also known as *datasets*).  
   * **High Permission Users** — choose a team or role with broad access.

### **Access via Ownership**

Using Team tags and/or service ownership information, access is divided so people can edit or see the content for which they're responsible.

For assets, owners get highest access (Editor), while others get either Viewer or No Access.

For data, owners get View access, while others get No Access.

Policy names are auto-applied in the format *"\[Product Name\] Ownership."*

### **Sensitive Data Partition**

1. Under **Choose Data Scope**, select a product with **In Product**, then narrow the scope with **Tagged** by choosing a key and its values. Use **New Product** to add another product to the same partition.  
2. Under **Designate Users with Access**, add the roles or teams that may access this data.  
3. Enter a **Name** for the policy.

### **High Permission Users**

For Data, you can select user groups that won’t be restricted from viewing any data.

A similar concept is now available for Assets \- you can select user groups that will always have highest access.

## **Limitations**

All of the following items are on our roadmap.

### **Limited number of supported products**

For Owner-based data access, we support Logs, RUM, APM, and Cloud Cost, with more on the way.

For Owner-based asset access, we support dashboards and monitors, also with more on the way.

### **Untagged data is hidden by default**

Data that is not tagged with a team is hidden from everyone except High Permission User Groups. For example, if you enable Logs Ownership Access and some log events do not have a `team:{team}` or recognized `@team` value, those events are hidden from non-high-permission users until they are tagged or access is otherwise granted.

### **Ownership is resolved via team tags only**

Ownership is currently determined from team tags: `team:{team}` for assets and data, and recognized `@team` values for supported data. Additional ownership resolution mechanisms, such as custom owners, are planned but not yet available.

### **Sensitive Data Partitions cannot be created for products with Owner-based policies**

You cannot create individual Sensitive Data Partitions when a product already has an Owner-based policy configured. Conversely, you cannot enable an Owner-based policy while individual Datasets exist.

### **API and Terraform support are not available**

During Preview, configure Owner-based policies in the Access Control UI. API and Terraform support are not available for Owner-based policies.

### **No Preview & Diagnostics**

A preview feature to help you understand the access impact of Owner-based policies before enabling or changing a policy is planned but not yet available.

### **Downtime Access Controls Preview isn’t fully compatible**

There’s another live Preview feature to help users control who can mute a monitor. You can ignore this if you’re not enrolled into this. Please contact us if you do, we’ll share the limitation details.
